title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down. It opens with a question: how can one define directly an integrable connection (the Gauss–Manin connection) on R^i f_*(Ω^•_{X/S})? The rest of the page sets up a general gluing lemma that would answer it.

Lemma (sketched). Data:
- X a topos, K^•, L^• complexes of abelian sheaves on X.
- 𝒰 a sheaf of groups with a homomorphism 𝒰 → Hom^•(K,L)^{-1} = ∏_i Hom(K^i, L^{i-1}), the sheaf of degree −1 maps (homotopies).
- P a 𝒰-torsor.
- θ: P → Z Hom^•(K,L)^0, the sheaf of chain maps K → L.
- θ is equivariant up to homotopy: θ(g·p) = θ(p) + d∘g + g∘d =: θ(p) + δ(g).

Conclusion: there is a well-defined morphism φ = φ(𝒰,P,θ): K → L in D(X) (perhaps already in the homotopy category 𝒦(X)). Its listed properties are:
1) φ is functorial in L (and presumably in K).
2) φ is compatible with change of structure group 𝒰 → 𝒰', with P' induced from P and θ = θ'∘u.
3) Presumably: if P has a global section p, then φ is the class of θ(p).

How φ is built. Over a cover where P has local sections p_α, the chain maps θ(p_α) differ by δ(g_αβ), where g_αβ is the transition cocycle. Since 𝒰 → Hom^{-1} is a homomorphism into an abelian group, these homotopies satisfy the cocycle condition strictly. So the local maps glue to a map K → Č(𝒰_α, L) ≃ L, i.e. a morphism in D(X), independent of choices.

Intended application. Locally on X, a tangent vector field on S lifts to X. The possible liftings form a torsor under the vertical tangent sheaf T_{X/S}. Each lift gives a Lie-derivative chain map on Ω^•_{X/S}. Changing the lift by a vertical field ξ changes this map by d∘ι_ξ + ι_ξ∘d, by Cartan's homotopy formula. The lemma then yields a global morphism in D, hence the Gauss–Manin connection on R^i f_*, defined 'directly' without crystals or the Katz–Oda filtration. The page sits between notes on Dieudonné-module duality (previous page) and on characters of Barsotti–Tate groups (next page), so it is a side remark in the crystalline/BT project.
errors: The lemma is only sketched: hypotheses and properties are partly crossed out, and the statement is incomplete (item 3 is unfinished).

The text does not specify whether φ lives in 𝒦(X) or D(X). Gluing generally requires passing to a Čech/derived replacement of L, so D(X) is the right target. Independence of the cover and of the sections is not checked on the page.
Because the target Hom^{-1} is abelian, 𝒰 acts only through its abelianization. The group structure of 𝒰 plays no real role beyond giving a torsor class mapped into H^1(X, Hom^{-1}).

ideas.what: Seeking a direct (non-crystalline) definition of the Gauss–Manin connection on R^i f_* Ω^•_{X/S}
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection via local lifts of vector fields and Lie derivatives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Oda (1968); Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (1970); crystalline version Grothendieck/Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Crystalline construction in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); the direct Lie-derivative construction is not his published approach

ideas.what: Gluing locally defined chain maps, parametrized by a torsor and differing by homotopies δ(g)=dg+gd, into a global morphism in the derived category
ideas.modern_name: Descent of morphisms in D(X) via Čech gluing / twisting by a torsor; Cartan homotopy formula
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; standard in Katz 1970, Illusie, Deligne

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but standard gluing lemma aimed at the Lie-derivative/Cartan-formula construction of the Gauss–Manin connection, which appears in Katz (1970) and is folklore. It is mildly interesting as evidence that Grothendieck sought a non-crystalline direct definition around 1969, but there is no new mathematics.

Item 2 concerns a morphism u: 𝒰 → 𝒰' with P' induced from P and θ = θ'∘u (transcribed as 'θ = uθ'').
Item 3 likely begins 'si P admet une section p ...' (i.e. φ = θ(p)).
